entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Aimone Taparelli (died August 15, 1495) was a prominent Italian Roman Catholic priest and a dedicated member of the Order of Preachers, whose career significantly shaped the late medieval religious landscape of northern Italy. Operating primarily in the Lombard and Liguria regions, Taparelli served as an Inquisitor-General for his order, a role that placed him at the forefront of the Church's efforts to maintain doctrinal purity and suppress perceived heresies during a period of intense religious and social change. His work provides a valuable lens into the operational mechanisms of the Dominican Inquisition and its regional impact.

Taparelli's core activities centered on his dual roles as an Inquisitor-General and a travelling preacher. As Inquisitor-General, he wielded considerable ecclesiastical authority, responsible for investigating, prosecuting, and adjudicating cases of suspected heresy. This involved a complex legal process, often including public sermons, interrogations, and the imposition of penances or, in severe cases, the handing over of individuals to secular authorities for execution. Simultaneously, he traversed numerous northern Italian cities, delivering sermons aimed at reinforcing Catholic orthodoxy, combating popular superstitions, and inspiring spiritual devotion among the populace, thereby extending the Dominican Order's influence beyond formal inquisitorial procedures.
